findings.comment: Direct line of sight from transformers to meters not verified. Provide line of sight analysis or building sections confirming unobstructed visual path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter location(s), or provide documented AE Design approval for exceptions.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations and corresponding meter locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. Meters are shown on the exterior of all eight buildings. The four transformer pads are located in various positions around the site (near Buildings 1, 2, 4, and 7). While the 2D schematic plan shows the general proximity of transformers and meters, it is impossible from a top-down plan view to determine unobstructed visual line of sight. The site has buildings, landscaping, retaining walls, sidewalks, and other vertical obstructions that could block the line of sight between some transformers and their serving meters. For example, the transformer south of Building 4 to the meters on Building 4 might be blocked by the building itself depending on building geometry and roof configuration.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformers to be in direct line of sight to meters. This requires not only proximity but also unobstructed visual path from the transformer to the meter location. A 2D plan cannot adequately verify line of sight. Building sections, 3D visualization, or explicit note from AE Design confirming line of sight verification is needed. Without this verification, it is unclear whether all transformer-to-meter pairs meet the line of sight requirement.

findings.comment: Many meter locations on building faces do not have direct unobstructed line of sight to transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path. Meters on the east/west/south sides of buildings cannot see transformers on opposite sides. Provide: (1) Confirmation that all meters are relocated to faces that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer, OR (2) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units authorizing the non-line-of-sight meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple buildings and meter locations throughout site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to trace visual line-of-sight paths from transformer pads to meter locations. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because the meters are distributed on multiple exterior sides of the buildings (e.g., east and west walls) and the transformers are located at specific single points near the drive aisle, many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source. Therefore, many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer.' The four transformer pads are positioned at single points along the main drive loop (T1 west of Bldg. 2, T2 between Bldg. 4-5, T3 south of Bldg. 6, T4 west of Bldg. 8), while meters are distributed on multiple building faces (east side, west side, south side). Building structures physically obstruct the visual path from many meters to their source transformers.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 (Location of Meter Sockets) requires transformers to be 'within sight' of meter locations to enable Austin Energy personnel to 'verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' The Regulatory Overview for this grouping clarifies: 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' Line of sight means an unobstructed visual path - if a building structure blocks the direct view from meter to transformer, the line of sight requirement is not met. The vision analysis explicitly identified that 'many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source,' which necessarily means building structures obstruct the line of sight. AE personnel cannot verify connections and perform coordinated operations if they cannot see both the meter and the transformer from a single vantage point.

findings.comment: Transformer pads not in direct line of sight to meter location. Buildings and trees block visual path from transformer pad to meters.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads to associated meters on Buildings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows three transformer pads and eight building meters distributed around the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 determined that 'for most meters, there is no direct line-of-sight to a transformer pad. The buildings themselves obstruct line-of-sight, and the electrical routing often travels around the perimeters of the buildings to reach the meter banks.' Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not clearly label meter locations; vision analysis confirmed 'meters are not clearly marked on this site plan.' Additionally, vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that 'if meters were placed on the nearest walls, the visual path from the transformer pad would cross directly through the adjacent parking stalls (potentially blocked by parked cars) and the future canopy of the tree designated by the "Tree Well."' This indicates obstructions (vehicles and trees) would block line of sight.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires transformers to be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations. The site plan electrical design routes conduit around building perimeters rather than direct paths, buildings obstruct sightlines, and trees (tree wells shown adjacent to transformer pad) would block visual paths from transformers to meters. The lack of clearly marked meter locations on the primary site and electrical plans prevents verification of compliance. Obstructions from buildings and trees indicate non-compliance.

findings.comment: Provide building elevations and a site plan diagram showing sight lines between all electrical meters and their serving transformers, confirming that: (1) meters are located on first floor or ground level, and (2) unobstructed sight line exists from transformer to meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three transformer pads located on the property: (1) One west of Building 2; (2) One west of Building 8; (3) One centrally located in the courtyard between Buildings 4-7. Electrical meters are mounted on building walls for all eight buildings. However, the site plan does not provide line-of-sight verification or dimensional data showing the relationship between meter locations and transformer locations. Without building elevation drawings, it cannot be confirmed whether meters are on first floor/ground level relative to their respective serving transformers or whether sight lines between meters and transformers are maintained (unobstructed by buildings, walls, or other features).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires electrical meters to be located on first floor or ground level and within sight of the serving AE transformer. While the plan shows meters and transformers, it does not provide the elevation information (first floor vs. upper floors) or line-of-sight verification necessary to confirm compliance. Meters on a multi-story townhome building could potentially be on upper floors, and sight lines could be obstructed by other buildings or structures.

findings.comment: Electrical meters are shown on building exterior walls (Sheet 21), but no documentation is provided confirming that each meter is located on the first floor or ground level and within line-of-sight of its corresponding transformer. Provide notes or details on the electrical plan documenting the meter height and sight line relationship to each transformer.
applicableAreas: Building exterior walls where electrical meters are mounted in relation to transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies electrical meter locations on each building's exterior walls: Building 1 south side, Building 2 south side, Building 3 north side, Building 4 north side, Building 5 east side, Building 6 south side, Building 7 south side, and Building 8 south side. Blue branch lines connect from the main underground electric line network and transformer pads to these meter locations. However, the plan provides no dimension callouts, sight line indicators, arrows, or notes documenting that each meter location: (1) is on the first floor or ground level, or (2) is within sight of the corresponding transformer location as required. While transformer locations are shown separately from meter locations, no visualization or notation demonstrates the sight line relationship or confirms that meters are within line-of-sight of their respective transformers.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires that electric meters be located on first floor or ground level and within sight of the Austin Energy transformer. While Sheet 21 shows both meter and transformer locations on the site plan, it provides no documentation confirming that: (1) all meters are at first floor or ground level (the plan does not show building sections or elevations for meter height), or (2) sight lines from each meter to its transformer are unobstructed. Without specific notation, sight line diagrams, or elevation details confirming these requirements, compliance cannot be verified from the submitted plans. This is unclear because the available plan documentation is insufficient to confirm that the meter location requirements are being met.

findings.comment: Show and label all service disconnects on the electrical plan. Indicate their location relative to meters (grouped together per code requirements) and verify they are within 20 feet and line of sight of the meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows and labels eight meter locations on building exterior walls as 'Electrical Meters.' However, no disconnects are shown, labeled, or identified on the electrical plan. The grouping guidance specifies: 'Meters and disconnects must be grouped together in a common location... The disconnect must be grouped with the meter beside the AE transformer (adhering to transformer clearances per UCM § 1.10.4) or outside the building within line of sight of the transformer.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1 and 1.16.0, both meters AND disconnects must be shown and labeled on plans. The disconnect is where the customer's service is isolated from the utility service and is a critical safety component. Without showing disconnect locations, it cannot be verified that they are properly grouped with meters, within required distances, within line of sight of transformers, and accessible for emergency disconnection.

findings.comment: Meters and disconnects not labeled on all required sheets. Label all electrical meters and disconnects on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. For grouped metering, label the service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway location, and note the distance between meters and disconnects (maximum 20 feet, must be within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Specify meter specifications (single-phase, three-phase, main vs. sub-meter).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels meters as "Electrical Meters" with callout lines to building wall locations. Sheets 9, 19, and 31 do not show meters or meter labels. No callouts define meter specifications, disconnect locations, service distribution enclosure locations, or grouping configurations. For a multi-unit residential development, disconnect locations are not identified relative to meters.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 and § 1.16.0 require that plans clearly identify meter and disconnect locations. Meter labels and disconnect callouts enable Austin Energy to verify that the service configuration is accessible, properly grouped (if applicable), and compliant with spacing requirements (maximum 20 feet between meter and disconnect per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Without labels and callouts on the site, wet utilities, and landscape plans, the reviewer cannot confirm that the metering design meets code requirements across all plan disciplines.

findings.comment: Individual labels are required for all meters and disconnects. Assign unique identifiers to each of the 8 meters (e.g., 'M-1' through 'M-8' corresponding to Buildings 1-8) and to all pull boxes (e.g., 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.). Show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where meters appear. Create a meter schedule or specification table on the electrical plan showing meter identification, building served, location, and type.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meters labeled generically as 'Electrical Meters' and 8 pull boxes labeled as 'Electrical Pull Box' without individual identifiers. No unique labels (e.g., 'METER-1', 'METER-2', 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.) are provided. While the meters and pull boxes are positioned on the plan, they cannot be specifically referenced or correlated with building designations without individual identification. No specification table or notes section provides meter and disconnect information.
findings.reasoning: Each meter and disconnect must be individually labeled and identified so that: (1) it can be specifically referenced in specifications and coordination documents, (2) building service connections can be clearly traced, (3) service upgrades can be implemented with precision, and (4) inspectors can verify the correct equipment is installed. Generic labels are inadequate.

findings.comment: Building elevations or meter location detail sheets must be provided showing that electrical meters are NOT located on/under porches, stairways, overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or other prohibited locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1. Provide building elevations with meter locations clearly identified relative to architectural features.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters are mounted directly on building foundation walls for all eight buildings. However, the plan does not provide sufficient detail regarding the specific mounting locations relative to building architectural features. Visual positioning suggests meters are mounted on exterior sidewalls, but the plans do not explicitly indicate: (1) Whether any meters are located under porches, covered entryways, or overhangs; (2) The exact relationship to stairways (some buildings have units with stairs); (3) Whether any meters are located under carports or covered parking areas; (4) The relationship to accessible routes or ramps. Sheet 21 notation indicates building FFEs and unit numbers but does not detail these specific meter location constraints.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 prohibits electric meters from being located on/under porches, stairways, under overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or where moving objects might damage equipment. The site plan shows meters are wall-mounted but does not provide the architectural detail necessary to confirm they are not located under prohibited features. Meters appear to be on building sides, but without building elevation drawings or detail sections showing the relationship of meters to overhangs, carports, and architectural features, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Provide building electrical plans, riser diagrams, or service disconnect location drawings showing the distance between electrical meters and their serving main service disconnects, confirming distance does not exceed 20 feet and that meter and disconnect are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meter locations but does not show or reference electrical service disconnect switch locations. The electrical design plan does not identify where main disconnect switches or service disconnects are located relative to meters. Without this information, the distance between meters and disconnects cannot be verified from the available site plan documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires that the distance between electric meter and disconnect does not exceed 20 feet, and meter and disconnect must be within line of sight. The site plan does not show disconnect switch locations, making it impossible to verify this requirement from the available evidence. Building electrical plans or riser diagrams that show disconnect switch locations would be necessary to make this determination.

findings.comment: Meter location compliance with prohibited locations and flood elevation requirements is not demonstrated. Please provide: (1) architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to building porch/stairway/overhang obstructions; (2) 3-foot separation verification from gas meters (show gas meter locations if present); (3) elevation certificates or grading plan showing meters are minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level (or FEMA determination if in floodplain); (4) notes confirming meters are readily accessible and on first floor/ground level within sight of transformer.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows meters attached to building walls but does not provide documentation regarding: (1) flood elevation verification (meters must be minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level per UCM § 1.9.3.1), (2) clearance to gas meters (3-foot minimum per UCM § 1.9.3.1(C)(3)), (3) clearance to porches/stairways/overhangs >72 inches, (4) meter accessibility and location on first floor/ground level. Sheet 9 does not show meters at all. Facts.md indicates site is in FEMA Zone X (outside 100-year floodplain), but architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to buildings are not provided in the available documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 specifies meter location requirements: (1) outdoors, readily accessible, on first floor/ground level, within sight of transformer; (2) not on/under porches or stairways; (3) not under overhangs >72 inches; (4) minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood elevation; (5) minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters/regulators/relief valves. The plans show meters but do not verify compliance with these location restrictions. Without architectural elevations or detailed meter location callouts showing compliance, UCM § 1.9.3.1 compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: Transformer to meter line of sight distance may be excessive. Routing from western transformer pad to Building 3 appears to exceed 150 feet, potentially exceeding operational practice standards for 'within sight' requirement.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to distant meters
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan, scale 1" = 20') vision analysis measured distances along electrical routing paths: 'Based on the 1" = 20\' scale, distances vary significantly. For example, the distance from the western transformer pad to the Bldg 8 meters is roughly 30-40 feet, while the routing from that same pad to the Bldg 3 meters appears to be over 150 feet along the designated path.' The routing from the west pad to Bldg 3 meters is stated as 'over 150 feet along the designated path.' The vision analysis flagged that some routing distances exceed 150 feet, which is the operational practice standard for 'within sight' per the grouping regulatory overview.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires transformers to be 'within sight' of meters. The code does not specify a maximum distance. Operational practice, as noted in the grouping regulatory overview, suggests 150 feet as the maximum reasonable sight distance. The electrical routing from the western transformer pad to Building 3 meters is estimated at 'over 150 feet' along the path. This suggests potential non-compliance with operational practice standards for line-of-sight interpretation, though the code technically does not specify a maximum distance.

findings.comment: Electrical routing from public utility connection point to transformer and meters not verified as 100% on private property. Provide routing diagram or plan notes clearly indicating property line boundaries and confirming that all electrical routing from the initial public utility connection point through transformers to all meters is located entirely on private property and does not route through public ROW or public easements.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from public ROW entry point through transformer and meter locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) which shows blue electrical routing lines entering from Valley View Road (public right-of-way) on the left side of the plan. The routing line is labeled "Underground Electric Line" where it enters from the public ROW. The majority of the electrical routing network shown on the site appears to be within private property boundaries, but the entry point and initial routing segment from Valley View Road into the site are clearly shown originating in public ROW. The plan does not explicitly denote property line boundaries along the entire routing path to verify that the routing is 100% on private property after connection to the system.
findings.reasoning: Code requires electrical routing from riser to transformer and meter to be 100% on private property. Sheet 21 shows the electrical routing line entering from Valley View Road (public ROW). While most of the internal site routing appears to be on private property, the plans do not clearly verify that all electrical routing from the initial connection point is on private property and does not route through any public easement areas. The entry point in the ROW raises questions about whether initial segments comply with the 100% private property requirement.

findings.comment: Many meter locations shown on Sheet 21 are not within sight of transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path (see EL-14.38 findings). Provide: (1) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design AND Distribution Metering business units authorizing meter locations without direct line of sight to transformers, OR (2) Reposition all meters to locations that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer on first floor/ground level per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple meter locations throughout the site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 to identify meter locations and access. Vision analysis identified: 'Locations: Meters are explicitly labeled as Electrical Meters using text boxes with leader lines. The leader lines point directly to the exterior walls of the buildings. Locations include: West side of Bldg. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8; East side of Bldg. 1, 2, 4, 6, 8; South side of Bldg. 7.' All meters appear to be exterior wall-mounted locations with no indication on Sheet 21 that any meters are behind doors, in enclosed rooms, or elevated above ground level. Standard notation on electrical plans would explicitly indicate 'Meter Room' or location callouts if meters were not directly accessible. The notations appear to place meters on first-floor/ground-level building faces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 addresses 'Meters shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer, without written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units documented.' Two alternative compliance paths exist: (1) Meters are on first floor/ground level AND within sight of transformer (standard requirement), OR (2) Meters are not on first floor/ground level OR not within sight of transformer (exception scenario that requires written approval). The deficiency statement in EL-14.70 specifically addresses the exception case: 'when meters are shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer.' This triggers if either condition is not met. Vision analysis from EL-14.38 documented that 'many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer' because they are on opposite sides of buildings. This represents a failure of the 'within sight' requirement. The Regulatory Overview clarifies the requirement: 'Meter locations not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer require written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units.' The submitted plans show many meters without line of sight but provide no documented approval from AE Design or Distribution Metering. Therefore, EL-14.70 is a fail.
